title: Frontend: Cinema Hall
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Cinema Hall. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({reserved=[A2]}). Seats A1..A4 are buttons[data-seat=ID]; reserved seats are disabled. Other clicks toggle aria-pressed selection. Output [data-testid=total] is integer cents at 1000 per selected seat. Local selection does not reserve real inventory.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use stable seat IDs and separate reserved inventory from local selection.
alternativeApproaches: Design timed reservation holds with server authority and explain the race between two clients selecting the same seat.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Reserved seat; toggle selection; pricing category.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
